item.title: 2026 Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) Strategy Report: Executive Summary and Key Changes
item.category: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
item.description:
The Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) Strategy Report provides a comprehensive, annually updated evidence-based approach to asthma diagnosis, assessment, treatment, and prevention across the lifespan. Its central approach is personalized, iterative care based on the Assess-Adjust-Review cycle for both symptom control and reduction of future risk (including severe exacerbations, persistent airflow limitation, and treatment-related harm). GINA emphasizes objective confirmation of diagnosis wherever possible, and regular assessment of lung function, inhaler technique, adherence, multimorbidity, risk factors (including Type-2 biomarkers), and patient goals and preferences. GINA strongly recommends that all adults, adolescents, children and most preschoolers with asthma should receive inhaled corticosteroid (ICS)-containing treatment. GINA recommends against short-acting beta2-agonist (SABA)-only treatment. For adults/adolescents, GINA Track 1 using low-dose ICS-formoterol, an anti-inflammatory reliever (AIR), either as-needed-only (AIR-only) or as maintenance-and-reliever therapy (MART), is preferred because of its substantial reduction in severe exacerbations compared with SABA-based regimens, and its simplicity. Age-specific treatment pathways in children also emphasize ICS-containing therapy and exacerbation prevention. For difficult-to-treat and severe asthma, GINA provides structured guidance, emphasizing diagnostic verification, optimization of modifiable factors, inflammatory phenotyping, biologic therapy selection, and (as for all patients) systemic corticosteroid stewardship. Acute exacerbation care incorporates long-term preventive treatment, including post-discharge reassessment of management and action plan. Key 2026 updates include expanded AIR options for adults and children, revised guidance on severe asthma and selection of biologic treatment, and substantial updates to acute asthma management. GINA integrates evidence-based management with shared decision-making, self-management education, implementation, and global advocacy to reduce preventable asthma morbidity and mortality.

item.title: Individualized Treatment Effects of Cefepime vs Piperacillin-Tazobactam in Adults Hospitalized with Acute Infection
item.category: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
item.description:
Rationale: Among adults hospitalized with acute infection, a recent randomized trial observed no significant average treatment effect of cefepime versus piperacillin-tazobactam on acute kidney injury or death, but fewer days-alive-and-free-of delirium and coma with cefepime.

Objectives: To determine whether patients' individual characteristics modify the effect of cefepime versus piperacillin-tazobactam on outcomes.

Methods: In this secondary analysis of the Antibiotic Choice On Renal Outcomes (ACORN) trial, an effect model was derived and validated to predict the effect of cefepime versus piperacillin-tazobactam for adults hospitalized with acute infection. The primary outcome was survival without acute kidney injury; the secondary outcome was survival without delirium or coma.

Measurements and main results: The individualized treatment effect predicted in the validation cohort significantly modified the effect of cefepime versus piperacillin-tazobactam on survival without acute kidney injury (Qini 1.68; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.25-3.18; p-value = 0.01). Among 626 patients predicted to experience ≥5% benefit from cefepime, 81.2% of patients randomized to cefepime survived without acute kidney injury, versus 74.2% randomized to piperacillin-tazobactam (difference, 7.1%; 95%CI, 0.25 to 13.9%). Among 203 patients predicted to experience ≥5% benefit from piperacillin-tazobactam, 56.6% of patients randomized to cefepime survived without acute kidney injury, versus 63.0% randomized to piperacillin-tazobactam (difference, -6.3%; 95%CI, -20.7 to 8.2%). The effect of trial group on survival without delirium or coma was not modified by individual characteristics.

Conclusions: Patients' individual characteristics modified the effect of cefepime versus piperacillin-tazobactam on survival without acute kidney injury but not on survival without delirium or coma.

Qian ET, Graham Linck EJ, Spicer AB, Buell KG, Casey JD, Seitz KP
